status.label: Clarify Arabic key identity after save
status.detail: The screenshots show the source label changing from Arabic ب to / after save, but do not establish whether the remap behavior changed or only its layout-dependent display.

next_action.label: Confirm layout and saved-key behavior
next_action.reason: The active Arabic layout and whether the physical key still triggers the remap distinguish a display-label change from a source-key or text-mapping defect.

comment.body: Thanks for the before/after screenshots showing Ctrl+Alt+ب displayed as Ctrl+Alt+/ after saving. Which Arabic keyboard layout is active while you create and reopen the remap, and does pressing that same physical key after saving still trigger the mapped shortcut? Please also confirm whether you expect the physical key to remain mapped across layouts or expect the Arabic character itself to be emitted. Retest on PowerToys v0.102.3001 or newer if possible.

judgment.rationale: The screenshots document a real change in the displayed key label, but the report does not say whether the physical-key remap stops working or whether the desired behavior is character output. Current source stores remaps by virtual-key code and derives key names using the current thread's keyboard layout, so a layout-dependent label change is plausible without proving that the saved mapping changed.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.76.2 and includes one screenshot showing Ctrl+Alt+ب before save and another showing Ctrl+Alt+/ in the saved remap; it has no comments.

Current upstream at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 uses GetKeyboardLayout(0) and ToUnicodeEx when updating keyboard-layout key names, while MappingConfiguration stores single-key sources by virtual-key code.
The issue contains no expected-behavior description and does not report whether pressing the physical key after save still activates the mapping.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm the input layout used during capture and reopen, then test whether the same physical key still activates the saved shortcut before deciding whether the defect is display-only, source identity, or an expectation of text insertion.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys display or capture fix may apply if the label changes under the same active layout or if the physical source key no longer maps after saving. The current report only establishes the label change, so the candidate remains low-confidence.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep the captured Arabic shortcut key identity clear after saving
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The editor derives key names from the current thread's keyboard layout while the saved source is represented by a virtual-key code. Reopening under a different layout can therefore render a Latin name for the same key; the available screenshots do not establish whether the mapping itself changed.
plan: Confirm the active Arabic layout during capture and reopen, and test the saved mapping with the same physical key.
Compare the captured and reloaded source virtual-key values while switching between the Arabic and English input layouts.
If only the label changes, preserve or clearly display the captured key/layout identity in the saved editor row; if the source value changes, correct the capture and persistence path instead.
Keep key-to-key remapping distinct from Unicode text insertion and add regression coverage for save/reopen under Arabic and English layouts.
verification: A remap captured with the Arabic layout reopens with an unambiguous source identity under the same layout.
Switching layouts does not silently change which physical source key triggers the saved remap.
Existing virtual-key remaps continue to display and trigger correctly.

confidence.rationale: The source code can render names from the active layout and the screenshots show a changed label, but there is no current-build result or confirmation that the physical mapping fails.

issue_context.summary: A shortcut captured with the Arabic key ب is shown as / after saving, but the report does not establish whether only the displayed label or the actual remap changes.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.76.2 and provides screenshots of Ctrl+Alt+ب before save and Ctrl+Alt+/ in the saved row.
The issue has no comments and does not specify the active Arabic layout, expected behavior, or whether the physical key still activates the mapping after save.
Current upstream at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 updates key-name mappings using GetKeyboardLayout(0) and ToUnicodeEx; saved single-key remaps are keyed by virtual-key code.
inferences: The Latin slash label may be a layout-dependent name regenerated from the stored virtual key rather than a changed remap, but this is not confirmed.
If the expected behavior is to emit the Arabic Unicode character rather than map the physical key, that is different from the current key-to-key remapping behavior.
issue_context.analysis: The supplied screenshots are useful evidence of label normalization, not proof of a broken key event. The active input layout, saved source identity, and post-save behavior are needed to distinguish a display issue from a mapping defect or a request for text insertion.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and both supplied screenshots from the saved evidence; no public comments or linked fix were present.
Inspected keyboard_layout.cpp and its LayoutMap implementation at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368: key-name generation uses the current thread layout and ToUnicodeEx.
Inspected MappingConfiguration::AddSingleKeyRemap at the same revision: a single-key source is stored by virtual-key code rather than as a Unicode character.

information_gaps.information: The Arabic keyboard layout active during capture and reopen, whether the same physical key still triggers the saved remap, and whether the expected target is a physical key or Arabic character output
information_gaps.why_needed: These facts distinguish a layout-dependent display label from a changed source mapping or a text-insertion expectation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On PowerToys v0.102.3001 or newer, create and reopen the remap with the Arabic input layout active, then test the same physical key and report the intended behavior.
